szoveg_eredeti:
Families and small businesses need reliable electricity, especially during extreme weather. Compute campuses can help by reducing their power use when the grid is under strain.

Today we’re announcing the Grid Protectors Program. We’ll work with utilities, regulators and policymakers to develop practical ways for our future self-build campuses to reduce demand during periods of grid stress. Where local conditions, equipment and utility arrangements allow, we’ll also explore supplying power from on-site generation or storage and smoothing changes in demand.

Our agreement with Georgia Power is a starting point. For our planned campus in Effingham County, we’ve committed to pay the full infrastructure and electric-service costs required to serve the project. The agreement also includes up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response, allowing the utility to reduce electricity delivered to the campus when needed.

Flexibility complements investment in new energy supply and transmission. Our goal is to help make the grid more reliable while paying the costs our campuses create.
